title: Einstein's 1923 paper saying general relativity fits with the ether
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Einstein's 1923 paper saying general relativity fits with the ether, about 1923 at an unknown place, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

plain: This story is about the ether, an old idea of an invisible substance filling all of space, which most physicists dropped in the early 1900s. A podcast host named Jesse Michels says that in 1923 Albert Einstein wrote a paper saying his theory of gravity, general relativity, actually fits with the ether. People raise it because, if true, it would mean the idea of a space-filling medium was never fully ruled out, which matters for some theories about unusual propulsion. A second teller, Salvatore Pais, a Navy scientist who holds patents on unusual craft, tells it on the same show. He also says Einstein was against the idea for a long time and yet brought it back in a paper. Pais dates that paper to 1921, not 1923. So the story comes from the host's own framing and from a scientist guest, and they disagree on the year.
